steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13 inch baking dish.

Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Once the water is boiling, stir in the shell pasta, and return to a boil. Cook the pasta uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the pasta has cooked through, but is still firm to the bite, about 13 minutes. Drain well in a colander set in the sink.

Place turkey and stuffing in food processor, and pulse until finely ground and combined. Place the ground turkey and stuffing mixture in the bowl of a stand mixer along with the cream cheese, Parmesan cheese, mayonnaise, and 2 cups of the mozzarella. Mix with paddle attachment on medium-low until well blended.

Spread 1/2 cup of gravy on the bottom of the prepared dish. Stuff the pre-cooked pasta shells with the turkey mixture and place in the dish in tight rows. Top with the remaining gravy and the remaining 2 cups of mozzarella cheese.
Bake, covered, for 45 minutes. Uncover and cook for an additional 10 minutes until top is browned and bubbly. Allow to cool for 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Thanksgiving Leftovers Stuffed Shells
raw_recipe.description: This recipe sounds odd, but I promise it makes for an unbelievable, rich hearty meal! Family and friends all show up a couple days AFTER Thanksgiving knowing this will be on the menu... Cheesy and delicious, and feeds a crowd!

video.description: Turn all your Thanksgiving leftovers into totally tempting comfort food with this mouthwatering stuffed shell recipe. Mix leftover turkey and stuffing with cream cheese, Parmesan cheese and mayo. Stuff this savory mix into jumbo pasta shells and top with gravy and mozzarella. Then just try to resist when it arrives hot from the oven, all bubbly, beautifully browned, tempting with meat, cheese and Thanksgiving goodness.

review.reviewBody: This recipe does sound a bit odd but I gave it a try and everyone loved it! I added some leftover corn casserole and it was delicious.

I love the thought of casseroles. But my family isn't big on them. So when I decided to make this one I figured it would be another "just okay" casserole. Whoa, was I surprised. This is AWESOME! I didn't have Jumbo Shells so I made it with manicotti. I just used my handheld food chopper to chop up the turkey and dressing. Then tossed it into my stand mixer. Next my husband had the brilliant idea of putting the mixture into a sandwich bag and snipping off the corner, making filling the pasta super easy! It wAS FABULOUS! I like bread dressing for Thanksgiving so that's what we had today for this recipe. I can't wait to try this again with cornbread dressing...I bet it is great as well. My husband says we should try it again when we roast a chicken. Thanks so very much Abbeydave for something different to make with all those leftovers!!!

I thought this mixture of flavors was surprisingly good and I have used a version of it with some adjustments for probably close to 10yrs now. Honestly, I quit stuffing pasta because of how much time it adds to prep and ended up making thanksgiving lasagna. And if you use ready to use lasagna sheets, no need to boil the pasta, you saved an additional 20min or so. I enjoy cooking, but with 2 toddlers and a special needs teenager, I try to make things quick and easy where I can too. Half of the ingredients listed, I didn't care for, but I trusted the process and it made a flavor of it's own. I've also made it with chicken and it was good.

I simplified the recipe by using cooked macaroni and then I mixed it with the mixture of cheeses and turkey. Of course it was dry so I added milk to get the right consistency. I put the entire mixture into a casserole dish, topped with the last 2 cups of mozzarella cheese and baked.

It had a wonderful flavour and this way you can use whatever pasta you have on hand. No need to buy and stuff shells.

Made this again after Christmas and it's still a hit. Used stove top stuffing and a package of gravy mix because I didn't have enough leftovers of either. Also used cannelloni shells and as another reviewer suggested, I added a can of cream of mushroom soup to the base, and added a bit into the gravy on top. You can't even tell it's there! It was really good, everyone liked it a lot. It got better reviews than the enchiladas I made!

What's not to love about this recipe! Ok I didn't have shells so I used 12oz of elbows, so i made a layered pasta/turkey casserole. Cooked elbows and divided in 2, also I didn't processed everything in the blender. I chopped everything and mixed with a spoon. Layered gravy, pasta, turkey stuffing cheese mix, pasta, gravy, cheese. It was a great meal after snowshoeing! My son even went back for second instead of cookies for evening snack.... :) I do think tho that it's only as good as your original gravy and stuffing were.

The great reviews encouraged me to try this. To be honest, the family and I were underwhelmed - it was bland tasting; had a mushy, unpleasant texture; and was too salty. Unlikely to try it again, but if I did, I would omit the parmesan cheese ( too salty); rough chop and hand mix the stuffing and turkey to give it some texture; and kick it up with some garlic, red pepper and fried onions. I would also pass on the gravy and use a white sauce, maybe a cream soup undiluted.
Loved it! My only change would be a little less cheese (maybe 2c total mozzarella, instead of 4). It was very cheesy & good!

Other commenters suggested not to use a food processor -- I agree. Just chop and don't over mix for a nice texture. Leftover gravy?!! Never at my house. If you need to use gravy in a jar, be sure and add spices to it to insure great flavor. This was delicious. Maybe it's just me, but it always takes me a lot longer to prep any recipe than it says it should.

Like others I was skeptical but I was wanted to try something different. We were pleasantly surprised on how good this turned out. Like others I didn't process the turkey and stuffing just mixed them right in. I also cut back on the mozzarella to one cup at the end. The dish was hearty and delious.

I didn't have a stand mixer or paddle attachment so I had to mix everything by hand and it was slightly difficult. Next time I will wait for the cream cheese to soften a bit. I also used mild cheddar instead of mozzarella and 2 cans of Cream of Chicken soup (1/2 cup on the bottom & the rest on top) as we really like sauce in this house. Some corn would have gone a long way in adding flavor, but over all this was a really good leftover recipe!

I've made these shells two or three times now. I can only manage maybe one open-faced turkey sandwich after Thanksgiving, so I make these and put a few pans in the freezer for another day. They're awesome! My husband loves them so much he bragged to his co-workers and promised to take a pan to them for lunch. Unfortunately I only had one little pan left as we had already devoured the two larger pans, so now they'll have to wait until we have another turkey (not this year!) I never have enough gravy left over, so I just use whatever packets or jar I might have on hand. It doesn't matter what flavor gravy, it's always good!

This is a great recipe for leftover turkey! In fact, it's the best we've ever made and I plan to save it for each turkey dinner in the future. We just shared a turkey dinner at our daughter's house and, while cleaning up, I told her about this and how good it is so now I have to sign off here as I promised to e-mail it to her asap. Thanks a bunch for making me look like an awesome cook!
I was skeptical, but it was delicious! Made as directed.
Will definitely make this again.
The taste and texture was reminiscent of a tuna casserole. Very one-note dish. Not a hit in my family.
Made these for a luncheon and everyone loved them
I made this to the exact recipe. Have no idea what went wrong but it was aweful. Too rich and salty for me. Will not be making this again. Threw out most of it.

There are several recipes on here that are nonsense to see if baffoons will make them or even better leave a good review. Makes me laugh every time. I have given this one 3 stars for the sheer ridiculousness of it and that over 60 people fell for it. good job.

OMG!!! This was awesome! I didn't have enough gravy, so I used the little bit of gravy I had on the bottom of the pan and Cream of Mushroom soup on top. It would have been even more awesome with all gravy! Definitely keeping this for all future holiday leftovers.
